detected_by: harness refusal message: 'a worktree-isolated agent's git operations must target its own worktree' on a later git -C call, followed by manual pwd/log verification of the true worktree default cwd
impact: Approx 15 tool calls' worth of research reads and one cargo build/run executed against the shared checkout instead of the isolated worktree; one git reset --hard run there without a prior git status check. No confirmed data loss (content identical at same commit, own worktree already correct), but the shared checkout's branch state was altered without verifying it was safe to do so.
resolution: Stopped using any cd/-C targeting the shared checkout path; verified own worktree was already correctly based at 1fbc11887 with clean status; continued all further work using the default (worktree) cwd only.
summary: Wave-17 spell/companion/class_feature lane agent ran read/build commands (git reset --hard, cargo build/run, file reads) via 'cd /home/ubuntu/workspace/repos/codex && ...' which targets the SHARED main checkout, not the agent's own isolated worktree, because Bash cwd resets to the worktree default between calls but a cd inside one call executes there for that call only. Own worktree turned out to already be correctly based at 1fbc11887 (clean), so no work was lost, but the shared checkout's HEAD/working tree was mutated by an unreviewed 'git reset --hard' without checking its status first, violating shared-checkout git discipline. Harness began refusing further shared-checkout-targeted git ops mid-session.
